fields.title: Settings shows the Internal Work Orders toggle, off, with its description
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a new organization in which the Internal Work Orders setting has never been switched on.
fields.custom_steps: 1. Open Settings > Work Orders.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • A toggle "Internal Work Orders" shows on the tab, written in Title Case like the other toggles.
  • The toggle is off.
  • Its description reads "Lets you flag your own company as an internal customer and mark a customer's work order, or a single line of a billable work order, as No Charge (warranty, goodwill, comeback). Internal and no-charge work orders close without an invoice; their parts cost posts to the expense account of their category instead of Cost of Parts."

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories), story SV-11766 (Story 9, Reports, dashboard and exports)

  • S1-R1: “Settings > Work Orders shows a toggle "Internal Work Orders" (Title Case like the other toggles on the tab), off by default, organization-wide like the other toggles, with the description "Lets you flag your own company as an internal customer and mark a customer's work order, or a single line of a billable work order, as No Charge (warranty, goodwill, comeback). Internal and no-charge work orders close without an invoice; their parts cost posts to the expense account of their category instead of Cost of Parts."”
  • Feature Overview: “Two kinds of work order, one way to close them.”
  • Terminology: “Internal Work Orders → the name of the setting under Settings > Work Orders and of the report under Reports; both cover internal and no-charge work orders, as does the Technician Efficiency chip "Internal work orders: Hide / Only internal / Show all" (tooltip "Internal and no-charge work orders", S9-R3). On a flagged customer's work order the badge reads Internal, never No Charge.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

Compare the screen with the pictures; the expected results come from the PRD.

fields.title: First turn-on opens the customer picker window with Save disabled
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a new organization in which the Internal Work Orders setting has never been switched on.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open Settings > Work Orders.
  2. Switch the "Internal Work Orders" toggle on.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The toggle "Internal Work Orders" is off.

Step 2:

  • A window titled "Which customers are your own company?" opens.
  • It has a customer picker with search, and no customer is picked.
  • Under the picker the hint reads "Pick up to 50 customers here. Flag more from Edit Customer."
  • The line "You can change this any time: Customers > Edit Customer > Internal customer." shows.
  • It has the buttons "Do this later" and "Save"; "Save" is disabled.
  • The window lists no customer as already flagged.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories)

  • S1-R2: “Switching the toggle from off to on for the first time in the organization opens the modal "Which customers are your own company?" with the body "Work orders for these customers are internal: no prices and no invoice; parts cost posts to the expense account of their category when you use QuickBooks or AccountingHub. Nothing is picked for you: your location is not always a customer, and the names can differ. Pick one or more, or do it later from the customer page.", a customer picker (the standard customer Select with search, several customers can be picked, each shown as a chip with a remove control; up to 50, with the hint "Pick up to 50 customers here. Flag more from Edit Customer."), the line "You can change this any time: Customers > Edit Customer > Internal customer." and the buttons "Do this later" and "Save". No customer is preselected. Save is disabled until at least one customer is picked. Save saves the toggle (on) and flags the picked customers in one step (only this toggle and the flags; other unsaved changes on the tab wait for Save settings; to back out, the user switches the toggle off and saves settings), closes the modal and then shows the dialog of S1-R11 for each picked customer with open billable work orders, one after another; the page shows the toggle on and the hint line of S1-R3 with nothing left to save for this setting. Closing the modal with X acts as "Do this later" (S1-R5); Esc and a click outside do nothing, as in every dialog of the app. The modal is shown once per organization: switching the toggle on again later opens nothing (S1-R10). Switching it off opens nothing. The modal never lists who is flagged, and Settings > Work Orders never lists customers.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “First-time modal, more than 50 customers | "Pick up to 50 customers here. Flag more from Edit Customer." | Hint under the customer picker (S1-R2)”
  • Story 1, Entry points: “Not on New Customer, not in a Settings list and not on the work order itself: a work order becomes internal only through its customer. Removing the flag: unticking the checkbox (S1-R6), allowed any time with the info dialog of S1-R12. Who is flagged is visible on the Customers list and the customer header (S1-R8), not in Settings.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

Compare the screen with the pictures; the expected results come from the PRD.

  • iwo-happy-02-02-pick-your-internal-customers.png

fields.title: Picking two customers and Save turns the setting on and flags both
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a new organization in which the Internal Work Orders setting has never been switched on.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A with no open work orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B with no open work orders.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open Settings > Work Orders.
  2. Switch the "Internal Work Orders" toggle on.
  3. Type customer A's name in the customer picker.
  4. Pick customer A.
  5. Type customer B's name in the customer picker.
  6. Pick customer B.
  7. Click Save.
  8. Open the Customers list.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The toggle is off.

Step 2:

  • The "Which customers are your own company?" window opens.

Step 3:

  • Customer A is offered.

Step 4:

  • Customer A shows as a chip with a remove control.
  • "Save" becomes enabled.

Step 5:

  • Customer B is offered.

Step 6:

  • Customer B shows as a second chip with a remove control.

Step 7:

  • The window closes.
  • The toggle shows on.
  • The hint line shows under the description.
  • Nothing is left to save for this setting: leaving the page asks nothing about unsaved changes for it.

Step 8:

  • Customer A and customer B each show an "Internal" badge next to their name.

  • The customer header shows an "Internal" badge next to customer A's name.

Step 5:

  • Customer A's row shows the "Internal" badge next to its name.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories)

  • S1-R7: “Edit Customer shows the checkbox "Internal customer" as the last field of the dialog, below "PO is required", with the helper "Work orders for this customer are internal: no prices, no invoice, parts cost posts to the expense account of the internal category." When ticked, the select "Default internal category" appears under it, listing the active Internal categories, General Internal preselected, with the helper "Used by every new internal work order for this customer unless the asset has its own category." It is shown while the setting is on (S1-N4 for the exception). New Customer does not show it: a customer is flagged after it exists, from Edit Customer or the modal. The checkbox and the modal are the only places the flag is set; ticking it on Save flags the customer (with the dialog of S1-R11 when open billable work orders exist).”
  • S1-R8: “While the setting is on, a flagged customer shows an "Internal" badge next to its name in the customer header, in the customers list and on the customers list mobile card. While the setting is off the badge is hidden in all three places (S1-N4); the badges on work orders stay (S2-R10).”
  • S1-R11: “When a customer is flagged (Save in the modal, or on Edit Customer with the checkbox ticked), or the setting is turned on again while flagged customers have open billable work orders (S1-R10), a dialog reads "[n] open work orders for [customer] are billable. Make them internal? Prices, fees and discounts are removed; costs and hours are kept." and lists those work orders under the body, one line each (number, location, unit, status), at every location the user has access to, up to 10 rows and then "and [n] more". Counted as open: every billable work order of that customer that is not invoiced, not paid and not Declined, Estimates included. A row with a deposit carries the note "Deposit: stays billable"; a row with a posted vendor bill carries the note "Vendor bill: cost moves at Close" (no dialog of S2-R8 per work order on this path). Buttons: "Keep billable" and "Make internal". Make internal applies S2-R7 to every listed work order without a deposit; those with a deposit stay billable until the deposit is reversed and the dialog is shown again. Keep billable leaves them as they are; they finish with an invoice as today. Open no-charge work orders of that customer are not listed: they stay no charge with their category and keep Change category and Convert to Billable (S2-R6). With no open billable work orders the dialog is not shown. Saving Edit Customer for a customer that carries the flag shows this dialog again whenever that customer has open billable work orders, so work orders left billable earlier (a deposit since reversed, Keep billable, a user without 'Work Orders — Create & Edit') can be made internal later. Open billable work orders at locations the user has no access to are not listed; the line "[n] more at locations you don't have access to." under the list says how many, and they are converted when a user with access saves Edit Customer or the setting is turned on again (S1-R10). Make internal converts the listed work orders without switching location. A pending portal estimate of a work order made internal is no longer available: the portal refuses approval with "This estimate is no longer available." and shows the existing obsolete banner, since internal work orders are never on the portal (S2-R11).”
  • Key Decisions, Permissions (Action | Needs | Without it): “See the Internal badge on the customers list and the customer header | Customers page access | Not applicable”
  • Terminology: “Internal customer → one of the shop's existing customers flagged as the shop's own company or a sister company. Set in the modal that opens the first time the setting is switched on, or at the bottom of Edit Customer; nowhere else. Several allowed. Not a system customer: ShopView creates nothing.”
  • Feature Overview: “Internal work orders come from internal customers. Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories), story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S1-R11: “When a customer is flagged (Save in the modal, or on Edit Customer with the checkbox ticked), or the setting is turned on again while flagged customers have open billable work orders (S1-R10), a dialog reads "[n] open work orders for [customer] are billable. Make them internal? Prices, fees and discounts are removed; costs and hours are kept." and lists those work orders under the body, one line each (number, location, unit, status), at every location the user has access to, up to 10 rows and then "and [n] more". Counted as open: every billable work order of that customer that is not invoiced, not paid and not Declined, Estimates included. A row with a deposit carries the note "Deposit: stays billable"; a row with a posted vendor bill carries the note "Vendor bill: cost moves at Close" (no dialog of S2-R8 per work order on this path). Buttons: "Keep billable" and "Make internal". Make internal applies S2-R7 to every listed work order without a deposit; those with a deposit stay billable until the deposit is reversed and the dialog is shown again. Keep billable leaves them as they are; they finish with an invoice as today. Open no-charge work orders of that customer are not listed: they stay no charge with their category and keep Change category and Convert to Billable (S2-R6). With no open billable work orders the dialog is not shown. Saving Edit Customer for a customer that carries the flag shows this dialog again whenever that customer has open billable work orders, so work orders left billable earlier (a deposit since reversed, Keep billable, a user without 'Work Orders — Create & Edit') can be made internal later. Open billable work orders at locations the user has no access to are not listed; the line "[n] more at locations you don't have access to." under the list says how many, and they are converted when a user with access saves Edit Customer or the setting is turned on again (S1-R10). Make internal converts the listed work orders without switching location. A pending portal estimate of a work order made internal is no longer available: the portal refuses approval with "This estimate is no longer available." and shows the existing obsolete banner, since internal work orders are never on the portal (S2-R11).”
  • S2-R7: “Changing the customer on a work order works as today (not offered on an invoiced or paid billable work order, as today, nor on a closed internal or no-charge work order, S2-R9); until then the classification follows the new customer: to an internal customer the work order becomes internal (prices removed, costs and hours kept, no Convert actions); to a regular customer from an internal one it becomes billable (lines priced as in S2-R6). A No Charge mark and its category survive a change to another regular customer; a no-charge work order moved to an internal customer becomes internal and loses its category. The Change Customer dialog says what will happen to the prices and, when the work order stays internal or no charge, adds "Shop supplies resets to [customer]'s minimum ($[amount])." (without 'See Financial Data' the sentence omits the amount).”
  • Key Decisions: “Flagging a customer offers to make its open billable work orders internal; removing the flag is free and leaves open internal work orders internal.”
  • S2-R13: “The classification is written on the work order when it is created, when its customer changes and when it is converted; the closed record carries it too, with the category. Lists, reports and integrations read it from there, never from the customer flag. Converting to no charge or to billable, changing the category, a shop supplies amount change, Make internal (S1-R11, on each work order), Close with its posting date, Reopen, and adding or removing a customer's Internal flag are recorded in the work order or customer Audit Log with the user and the time.”

  • S1-R13: “Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders is a page with two tabs. Internal categories: columns Category (the default carries a Default badge), QuickBooks expense account (with the QuickBooks mark; "Not set" with a warning icon when empty), Internal customers using it, Work orders (count, all time; a billable work order with a no-charge line of the category counts too), and a row menu with Edit and Archive. The work order is created internal with the category resolved as: the asset's Internal category (S1-R15), else the customer's default (S1-R7), else the default Internal category; it is re-resolved while the work order is open when the asset changes or when the category of the asset or the customer is edited (a closed work order never changes), archived categories are skipped (S1-R16), and it can be changed on the asset or the customer, never on the work order. Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Work Order window opens.

Step 2:

  • At the bottom of the window, below the "Asset Here?" checkbox and a divider, an unticked "No Charge" checkbox shows with an info icon.

Step 3:

  • The tooltip reads "Warranty, goodwill or comeback work. Closes without an invoice; parts cost posts to the expense account of the category."

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R2: “In the New Work Order dialog (New Work Order only; Edit Work Order, which shares the dialog, is unchanged), picking a customer without the flag shows, at the bottom of the dialog below the "Asset Here?" checkbox and separated from it by a divider, an unticked checkbox "No Charge" with an info icon whose tooltip reads "Warranty, goodwill or comeback work. Closes without an invoice; parts cost posts to the expense account of the category." Ticking it reveals the required select "Category" listing the active No Charge categories, empty by default; Save is refused with the field message "Pick a category" until one is picked. When the category requires the original work order, the select "Original work order" appears under it (the customer's invoiced and closed work orders at the locations the user has access to, those on the same asset first, each as number, date and first line, and "Not in ShopView" under Other), optional here, with the helper "Which earlier work order this job comes from, or Not in ShopView, and the line on it. The line sets the original technician for the comeback and warranty numbers. Optional here, required at Close."; once a work order is picked, the optional select "Original line" lists its lines (number, title, technician). The checkbox is hidden when the selected customer is an internal customer and for users without 'See Financial Data'. Ticked, the work order is created No Charge with that category. It works whether or not any customer is flagged. As soon as a work order or a line is picked, the line "Original technician: [names]" (or "Original technician: none") shows under the selects, so a wrong attribution is seen and corrected by picking the line before anything is saved.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “No Charge info icon (New Work Order) | "Warranty, goodwill or comeback work. Closes without an invoice; parts cost posts to the expense account of the category." | Tooltip on the info icon”
  • Feature Overview: “No Charge is a mark with a category. A whole work order on a regular customer can be No Charge (the checkbox at creation, Convert to No Charge later, Convert to Billable back), and so can a single line of a billable work order (Mark as No Charge in the line's three-dots menu, or the No Charge checkbox in Edit Line and New Line; Story 12). Both carry one No Charge category from the shop's list (Warranty, Goodwill, Comeback to start, plus the shop's own) and, on categories that require it, the original work order the job comes from and, optionally, the original line on it, which sets the original technician. Categories are shop-managed: Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders holds two lists, Internal categories and No Charge categories; a category has a name, a QuickBooks expense account per connected location and, on No Charge, the flag Requires the original work order (on for Warranty and Comeback). Categories are archived, never deleted, so old work orders and reports keep theirs. The same accounts show on Settings > Integrations > QuickBooks > ShopView Accounts as one row per category; editing either place writes the same mapping. Nothing is created in QuickBooks.”

fields.title: Changing to an internal customer makes the work order internal
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, flagged as an Internal customer, with a Min shop supplies charge of $15.00.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, in status Approved, with one approved labor line of 2.0 hours.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click "Change Customer" on the customer card.
  3. Pick customer B.
  4. Confirm the change.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The Change Customer window opens.

Step 3:

  • The window reads "Prices are removed; costs and hours are kept."
  • It adds "Shop supplies resets to [customer B's name]'s minimum ($15.00)."

Step 4:

  • The work order shows the "Internal" badge.
  • The labor line shows 2.0 hours and no price.
  • The menu offers no "Convert to No Charge".
  • "Shop supplies" reads $15.00.

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-11767 (Story 10, Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders)

  • S2-R7: “Changing the customer on a work order works as today (not offered on an invoiced or paid billable work order, as today, nor on a closed internal or no-charge work order, S2-R9); until then the classification follows the new customer: to an internal customer the work order becomes internal (prices removed, costs and hours kept, no Convert actions); to a regular customer from an internal one it becomes billable (lines priced as in S2-R6). A No Charge mark and its category survive a change to another regular customer; a no-charge work order moved to an internal customer becomes internal and loses its category. The Change Customer dialog says what will happen to the prices and, when the work order stays internal or no charge, adds "Shop supplies resets to [customer]'s minimum ($[amount])." (without 'See Financial Data' the sentence omits the amount).”
  • S10-R2: “The amount can be changed on the work order until it is closed, with the existing per-work-order shop supplies control. Any customer change while the work order stays internal or no charge, or converting to no charge, resets it to the customer's Min. Making the work order billable again drops the flat amount and applies the customer's or the location's shop supplies rule as on any billable work order.”
  • Key Decisions, Permissions (Action | Needs | Without it): “Change the customer on a work order | 'Work Orders — Create & Edit' | As today”

From: "Internal Work Orders technical implementation plan", 2026-10-28, last updated 2026-11-10 (revision 5, built on PRD v1.0), sources/TECH-PLAN-Internal-Work-Orders-upload-2026-11-12.md, read 12 Nov 2026

fields.title: A vendor bill makes Convert to No Charge ask where the cost goes
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, in status Approved, with one special-order part, part 1, received against it and its vendor bill of $125.00 entered.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the work order's three-dots menu.
  3. Click "Convert to No Charge".
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The menu shows "Convert to No Charge".

Step 3:

  • First a window titled "Change where the cost is posted?" opens.
  • Its text reads "The vendor bill for [part 1] ($125.00) was posted to Cost of Parts. If you continue, that cost moves to [account] when this work order is closed."
  • Its buttons are "Cancel" and "Continue".

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly. [account] is the account the category picked in the next window is mapped to. [account] is not judged in this case: the category is picked only in the next window.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R8: “If a vendor bill already exists on the work order, a customer change (S2-R7), a Convert action (S2-R5, S2-R6) or, on a line that has a posted vendor bill, Mark as No Charge, Change category or Mark as Billable (Story 12) first shows the dialog "Change where the cost is posted?" with the body "The vendor bill for [part] ($[amount]) was posted to [account]. If you continue, that cost moves to [account] when this work order is [invoiced / closed]." For several bills: "The vendor bills for [n] parts ($[total]) were posted to [account]. ..." Buttons: Cancel and "Continue". The account names are the shop's own mapping rows (Cost of Parts, or the expense account of a category); between the expense accounts of two categories the dialog names both. Not shown when the location has no accounting integration.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Customer change, Convert or a line No Charge change with a vendor bill | "The vendor bill for [part] ($[amount]) was posted to [account]. If you continue, that cost moves to [account] when this work order is [invoiced / closed]." | Confirmation dialog, Cancel / Continue”

You can convert it to no charge again until it is invoiced." and the buttons Cancel and "Convert to Billable"; confirming removes the badge and the category, and every line comes back billable, including lines that carried their own No Charge mark before the work order was converted (S2-R5 replaced their categories; the advisor marks them again if needed), priced the way a new line on this work order would be priced that day: labor at the customer's labor rate, else the location's; parts from the pricing rules applied to the cost already on the line (the cost Close would post), not today's catalogue cost. Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R19: “No event writes a sell price onto an internal or no-charge work order, or onto a no-charge line (Story 12): not receiving a special-order part at a real cost, not editing the cost on a vendor invoice, not a core-charge change (today each of these derives or rewrites the part's sell price from the cost). Cost is written normally. The receive screen replaces its notice "Updating the cost also updates the sell price" with "Internal work order: cost only, no sell price" (or "No Charge work order: cost only, no sell price", "No Charge line: cost only"); the vendor-invoice item edit, which has no such notice today, gains the same cost-only notice for items on internal and no-charge work orders and lines. A sell price appears only on Convert to Billable or Mark as Billable, derived from the cost on the line at that moment (S2-R6, S12-R5).”
  • Key Decisions: “The books receive only what the shop paid for a part, never a derived sell price: no event writes a price onto internal or no-charge work (receive, vendor invoice, core charge), and Billable is the only moment a price is derived, from the cost on the line.”

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order)

  • S2-E7: “Parts with a core charge work as today up to resolution: the core row shows on the lines with no price, Core OK / Not OK is required before Close as it is before invoicing, and the completion wizard shows no core amount on an internal or no-charge work order. Not OK adds a charge to nobody; the vendor's core charge on the bill is cost and posts with the bill line (S7-R3). OK creates the vendor return as today, and its credit posts as in S7-R3a. Core cost is never part of Parts cost on the document or in the report. A stock part picked with its core posts both costs at Close, so the Stock parts row of the Finance tab posting summary (S3-R2) says what posts: "Stock parts $[amount], includes $[core amount] core cost · Posted to [account]"; the document and the report keep Parts cost without cores.”
  • S3-R3: “Close Work Order completes the work order if it is not yet Complete, creates the internal invoice underneath (carrying the work order number, nothing owed), relabels the picks to the internal invoice and sends their journal entries as invoicing does today (parts leave stock when they are picked), posts the entries of Stories 7 and 8, and shows the alert "Work order [number] is Closed · Internal." (or "Closed · No Charge."), with the X every alert in the app has. The work order shows the status Closed with its one badge (Internal or No Charge) and is locked as an invoiced work order is; underneath, the internal invoice is in the Closed state (Key Decisions). Every other effect of invoice creation applies: the snapshot in the work order history, the search index, the audit log; the exceptions are the ones listed in S3-R4 and the Customer PO rule of S3-R5. Adding a line to a closed work order spawns a new work order, as it does on an invoiced one today; the new one takes its customer's classification (S2-R1) and is billable on a regular customer. When the work order is not yet Complete, Close first runs the same completion steps as Create invoice today (tech stories, parts to pick, core decisions, parts to receive, and the missing details such as VIN, mileage and engine hours, per the organization's settings, in that order); the last button of that run reads "Close Work Order" and closes; the dialogs of S3-R2 open from it only in their two cases.”

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order)

  • S3-R3: “Close Work Order completes the work order if it is not yet Complete, creates the internal invoice underneath (carrying the work order number, nothing owed), relabels the picks to the internal invoice and sends their journal entries as invoicing does today (parts leave stock when they are picked), posts the entries of Stories 7 and 8, and shows the alert "Work order [number] is Closed · Internal." (or "Closed · No Charge."), with the X every alert in the app has. The work order shows the status Closed with its one badge (Internal or No Charge) and is locked as an invoiced work order is; underneath, the internal invoice is in the Closed state (Key Decisions). Every other effect of invoice creation applies: the snapshot in the work order history, the search index, the audit log; the exceptions are the ones listed in S3-R4 and the Customer PO rule of S3-R5. Adding a line to a closed work order spawns a new work order, as it does on an invoiced one today; the new one takes its customer's classification (S2-R1) and is billable on a regular customer. When the work order is not yet Complete, Close first runs the same completion steps as Create invoice today (tech stories, parts to pick, core decisions, parts to receive, and the missing details such as VIN, mileage and engine hours, per the organization's settings, in that order); the last button of that run reads "Close Work Order" and closes; the dialogs of S3-R2 open from it only in their two cases.”
  • S3-R1: “On an internal or no-charge work order, every place that offers "Create invoice" on a billable work order offers "Close Work Order" instead (Title Case, like Create Work Order, the same label everywhere) and closes it on that press, with no confirmation (as Create invoice runs today, SV-10312) apart from the two dialogs of S3-R2: the header button (on mobile, the icon button with the tooltip "Close Work Order"), the three-dots menu (only while it would hold Create invoice, S3-N2), the Create invoice action on the Finance tab, the finish action of the lines bulk bar, and the completion wizard of Simple Mode wherever it offers Create invoice (on these work orders the wizard shows no core amount and no "to invoice" wording). No path on these work orders creates a billable invoice. "Mark Reviewed" is unchanged.”

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order)

  • S3-R3: “Close Work Order completes the work order if it is not yet Complete, creates the internal invoice underneath (carrying the work order number, nothing owed), relabels the picks to the internal invoice and sends their journal entries as invoicing does today (parts leave stock when they are picked), posts the entries of Stories 7 and 8, and shows the alert "Work order [number] is Closed · Internal." (or "Closed · No Charge."), with the X every alert in the app has. The work order shows the status Closed with its one badge (Internal or No Charge) and is locked as an invoiced work order is; underneath, the internal invoice is in the Closed state (Key Decisions). Every other effect of invoice creation applies: the snapshot in the work order history, the search index, the audit log; the exceptions are the ones listed in S3-R4 and the Customer PO rule of S3-R5. Adding a line to a closed work order spawns a new work order, as it does on an invoiced one today; the new one takes its customer's classification (S2-R1) and is billable on a regular customer. When the work order is not yet Complete, Close first runs the same completion steps as Create invoice today (tech stories, parts to pick, core decisions, parts to receive, and the missing details such as VIN, mileage and engine hours, per the organization's settings, in that order); the last button of that run reads "Close Work Order" and closes; the dialogs of S3-R2 open from it only in their two cases.”

  • Terminology: “Closed · Internal / Closed · No Charge → how running text, the Finance tab, the success alert and the Reopen dialog name a closed internal or no-charge work order. On screen the status reads Closed and the one badge next to it reads Internal or No Charge, so the classification shows once. Underneath it is a work order with an internal invoice in the Closed state; the locks of an invoiced work order apply.”
  • Terminology: “Statuses are named as the app names them: Estimate, Approved, In Progress, Review, Complete, Invoiced, Paid and Declined. fields.title: Close runs the missing details step first and ends with Close Work Order
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location has no accounting integration (neither QuickBooks Online nor AccountingHub).
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the organization asks for the VIN before invoicing.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer, with one asset, asset 1, that has no VIN.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status In Progress, on asset 1, with all lines done.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the work order's three-dots menu.
  3. Click Close Work Order in the menu.
  4. Enter a VIN.
  5. Click the step's Close Work Order button.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The menu shows "Close Work Order".

Step 3:

  • A Missing Details step opens first and asks for the VIN.

Step 4:

  • The step's last button reads "Close Work Order".

Step 5:

  • Work order 1 closes with no other window: an alert reads "Work order [number] is Closed · Internal."
  • The status reads "Closed" with the "Internal" badge.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order)

  • S3-R3: “Close Work Order completes the work order if it is not yet Complete, creates the internal invoice underneath (carrying the work order number, nothing owed), relabels the picks to the internal invoice and sends their journal entries as invoicing does today (parts leave stock when they are picked), posts the entries of Stories 7 and 8, and shows the alert "Work order [number] is Closed · Internal." (or "Closed · No Charge."), with the X every alert in the app has. The work order shows the status Closed with its one badge (Internal or No Charge) and is locked as an invoiced work order is; underneath, the internal invoice is in the Closed state (Key Decisions). Every other effect of invoice creation applies: the snapshot in the work order history, the search index, the audit log; the exceptions are the ones listed in S3-R4 and the Customer PO rule of S3-R5. Adding a line to a closed work order spawns a new work order, as it does on an invoiced one today; the new one takes its customer's classification (S2-R1) and is billable on a regular customer. When the work order is not yet Complete, Close first runs the same completion steps as Create invoice today (tech stories, parts to pick, core decisions, parts to receive, and the missing details such as VIN, mileage and engine hours, per the organization's settings, in that order); the last button of that run reads "Close Work Order" and closes; the dialogs of S3-R2 open from it only in their two cases.”
  • S3-R1: “On an internal or no-charge work order, every place that offers "Create invoice" on a billable work order offers "Close Work Order" instead (Title Case, like Create Work Order, the same label everywhere) and closes it on that press, with no confirmation (as Create invoice runs today, SV-10312) apart from the two dialogs of S3-R2: the header button (on mobile, the icon button with the tooltip "Close Work Order"), the three-dots menu (only while it would hold Create invoice, S3-N2), the Create invoice action on the Finance tab, the finish action of the lines bulk bar, and the completion wizard of Simple Mode wherever it offers Create invoice (on these work orders the wizard shows no core amount and no "to invoice" wording). No path on these work orders creates a billable invoice. "Mark Reviewed" is unchanged.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

fields.title: Close records no payment and no receivable
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location has no accounting integration (neither QuickBooks Online nor AccountingHub).
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Complete, with one approved line with one stock part picked from inventory at a cost of $40.00 each, quantity 2, whose Shop supplies amount is $15.00.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Open the Finance tab.
  4. Open work order 1's log.
  5. Open customer A's Invoices tab.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The status reads Closed.

Step 3:

  • The Finance tab shows the document and no payment, balance or $0 payment.

Step 4:

  • The log has a Close entry where invoice created would be, and no "Invoice paid" entry.

Step 5:

  • Work order 1 is not listed.
  • Customer A's balance reads $0.00: the $15.00 of shop supplies is not charged.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order)

  • S3-R4: “No payment is recorded (not even the $0 payment a $0 invoice writes today) and no "Invoice paid" log entry is written, no customer transaction or receivable is created, no customer portal notification, email or invoice webhook is sent (the work order status webhook of Story 11 is), no invoice is sent to QuickBooks, the internal invoice is never listed in the Open API invoice lists and invoice.created and invoice.paid are never sent for it (both from the core release on, before Story 11), no tax, fee or discount is added, the shop supplies amount is not charged to the customer (it posts as an expense, Story 10), and the customer portal does not list the document (the portal vehicle list still counts a closed internal or no-charge work order for Last Service and Completed, as a service on the unit with $0.00 owed). Close and Reopen are recorded in the work order log as invoice created and reversed are today.”
  • S3-R6: “The asset Invoices tab lists the closed work order with status Closed, the badge, Total balance "No Charge" and Discount and Tax rate empty (rows on that tab have no actions). The customer's Invoices tab (the receivables ledger) does not list it; the customer's Work Orders tab does (S2-R10). GET /api/invoices/list leaves it out too (no screen uses it today). Customer statements, the customer balance and credit limit checks do not include it, and no message driven by an open balance can pick it up, since it carries none. The Finance tab menu of the closed work order offers Reopen Work Order only (S4-R1); Issue Credit is not shown, as there is nothing to credit.”
  • Goals: “A closed internal or no-charge work order creates no receivable, no payment and no customer message.”
  • Terminology: “Internal invoice → the record created by Close. It is a third invoice state, Closed, neither Invoiced nor Paid, with no customer transaction and no payment. It carries the work order number (as every invoice does today; no number is consumed or skipped), has nothing owed, and is never sent to the customer, the customer portal or an invoice webhook, nor listed in the Open API invoice lists; QuickBooks gets no invoice; AccountingHub receives it as a Closed record with no revenue (S8-R1). Its date is the posting date.”

fields.title: The NO CHARGE document of an internal work order shows cost and hours
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location has no accounting integration (neither QuickBooks Online nor AccountingHub).
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer, with one asset, asset 1.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, closed, on asset 1, closed with one approved labor line of 2.0 hours, one approved line with one stock part picked from inventory at a cost of $40.00 each, quantity 2, one special-order part billed at $125.00, whose Shop supplies amount is $15.00.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the Finance tab.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The masthead shows the letterhead left, the shop logo in the centre and "Internal Work Order [number]" with the date right.
  • Under the masthead line, on the left and not over the logo, the INTERNAL stamp shows with "Category: General Internal".
  • Bill to shows customer A; the asset block shows asset 1.
  • The labor line shows 2.0 hours only; the parts show quantity and cost only.
  • The Summary reads "Parts cost $205.00" ($80.00 + $125.00), "Shop supplies $15.00" and "Labor hours 2.0".
  • There is no tax, total, payments, balance or signature block.
  • The document offers "Download", "Print" and "Email".

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11767 (Story 10, Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders)

  • S3-R5: “The Finance tab of a closed work order shows the NO CHARGE document: the masthead as on the invoice today (letterhead left, the shop logo in the centre slot, the document block "Internal Work Order [number]" or "No Charge Work Order [number]" with the date right), and under the masthead line, on the left and never over the logo, the INTERNAL or NO CHARGE stamp with the line "Category: [name]" and, when set, "· Original work order [number]" (a link in ShopView, plain on the PDF), Bill to the customer, the asset block, labor lines with hours only, parts lines with quantity and cost only (cost under 'See Financial Data'), a Summary with Parts cost (one number: stock parts plus special orders and sublet, at the amounts of S3-R2, core cost excluded, S2-E7), Shop supplies (when above $0.00) and Labor hours (the labor hours on the lines), and no tax, total, payments, balance or signature block; with Download, Print and Email (the recipient field is empty; the user types the shop's own address or any other; never automatically). The Customer PO field is not required. The internal invoice carries the work order number, as every invoice does today; no number is consumed or skipped. Parts cost on the document and in the report is fixed at Close: a vendor bill entered, edited or deleted after Close posts its own amounts to the work order's expense account (S7-R3) and changes neither the document nor the report. Email uses the invoice email template of today (it carries no amounts) with the subject "Internal Work Order [number]" or "No Charge Work Order [number]".”
  • S10-R3: “The Finance tab posting summary (S3-R2) shows the row "Shop supplies $[amount]" with the note "Posted to [work order's expense account], credited to [shop supplies account]"; the shop supplies account is the income account of the existing "Shop supplies" item (Products And Services) in QuickBooks or the Shop supplies expense row in AccountingHub; the NO CHARGE document shows "Shop supplies $[amount]" in the Summary under Parts cost; the Internal Work Orders report shows it as a column (S9-R2).”
  • Terminology: “Hours → the labor hours on the lines of the work order, as the document shows them. The Finance tab posting summary, the NO CHARGE document and the Internal Work Orders report use them. Clocked hours per technician are in Technician Efficiency.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

fields.title: Reopen Work Order sits in the invoice menu where Reverse would be
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, closed.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 2, for customer B, invoiced, billable, so Reverse can be compared.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the Finance tab.
  3. Open the invoice menu on the Finance tab.
  4. Open work order 2.
  5. Open the Finance tab.
  6. Open the invoice menu on the Finance tab.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The header shows the "Closed on …" line and no Reopen button.

Step 2:

  • The document shows.

Step 3:

  • The menu offers "Reopen Work Order" and no "Issue Credit".

Step 4:

  • Work order 2 opens.

Step 5:

  • The document shows.

Step 6:

  • The menu offers "Reverse".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11761 (Story 4, Reopen a closed internal or no-charge work order)

  • S4-R1: “On a closed internal or no-charge work order the Finance tab's invoice menu shows "Reopen Work Order" where a billable work order shows "Reverse", and no Issue Credit. It is the only place to reopen; the work order header carries the line of S2-R9 and no button.”

fields.title: Reopen returns an internal work order to Complete with its shop supplies
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location has no accounting integration (neither QuickBooks Online nor AccountingHub).
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, closed, whose Shop supplies amount is $15.00.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the Finance tab.
  3. Open the invoice menu on the Finance tab.
  4. Click "Reopen Work Order".
  5. Click Reopen Work Order in the window.
  6. Open the Notes tab.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The document shows.

Step 3:

  • The menu offers "Reopen Work Order".

Step 4:

  • The window opens.

Step 5:

  • The status reads "Complete" with the "Internal" badge.
  • "Shop supplies" still reads $15.00.
  • The NO CHARGE document is gone from the Finance tab.
  • "Close Work Order" is offered again.
  • The page stays on the Finance tab.

Step 6:

  • A system note records the Reopen with the user and the time.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-11761 (Story 4, Reopen a closed internal or no-charge work order)

  • S4-R3: “Confirming reverses exactly the entries that were posted at Close (Stories 7 and 8), returns the parts to inventory as Reverse does today, removes the internal invoice, and sets the work order to Complete with its classification unchanged, the shop supplies amount kept, and the Convert and Change category actions offered again (S2-R9 applies only while closed or invoiced); the green message "Work order [number] reopened" confirms it, as the app confirms other finished actions. The reversal is dated the reopen date, so it is held only if that date's period is closed or missing (S4-E2 is corrected accordingly). Events for one work order are processed in order, one at a time: a Reopen arriving while the Close is Held turns the Close Dismissed; a Dismissed event is never retried and cannot be replayed by hand; a new Close waits while an earlier reversal for the same work order is Held, shown as Held with the reason "Waiting for an earlier held entry of work order [n]", so two Close entries are never posted without the reversal between them. The reversal credits and debits exactly the accounts the Close used.”
  • S2-R18: “Every classification change writes a read-only system note on the work order (Notes tab, author ShopView, with the user and the time) and an Audit Log row: Convert to No Charge ("Converted to No Charge by [user]. Category [name], original work order [number]. Prices, fees and discounts removed; costs and hours kept."), Change category (from, to, original work order kept or cleared), Convert to Billable ("Every line priced as a new line would be today. Category [name] removed."), Close (posting date, account), Reopen, and the line actions of Story 12 (S12-R6). Work order numbers in notes are links.”
  • S2-R13: “The classification is written on the work order when it is created, when its customer changes and when it is converted; the closed record carries it too, with the category. Lists, reports and integrations read it from there, never from the customer flag. Converting to no charge or to billable, changing the category, a shop supplies amount change, Make internal (S1-R11, on each work order), Close with its posting date, Reopen, and adding or removing a customer's Internal flag are recorded in the work order or customer Audit Log with the user and the time.”

From: "Internal Work Orders technical implementation plan", 2026-10-28, last updated 2026-11-10 (revision 5, built on PRD v1.0), sources/TECH-PLAN-Internal-Work-Orders-upload-2026-11-12.md, read 12 Nov 2026

  • Tech plan line 3400 (TP-473): “success → refetch, stay on Finance”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11762 (Story 5, QuickBooks Online account mapping), story SV-11767 (Story 10, Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders)

  • S5-R1: “Integrations > QuickBooks, ShopView Accounts, shows one row per category directly under Cost of Parts (above Cost of Goods (tax)), grouped under the headers "Internal work orders" and "No Charge work orders", each row named after its category and carrying the QuickBooks mark. A category the shop adds appears as a new empty row; an archived category keeps its row, greyed, with its mapping, and the row can still be remapped (a reopened work order still posts to its archived category, S12-E8). Under the rows a note reads "Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders are credited to the income account of your Shop supplies item in Products And Services; nothing to map here." Nothing is created in QuickBooks: the picker lists the location's existing expense accounts.”
  • S10-R5: “No new mapping row in either integration: QuickBooks credits the income account of the existing "Shop supplies" item (Products And Services) (Story 5, S5-R1 note); AccountingHub uses its existing "Shop supplies expense" row (Story 6).”
  • Terminology: “Category expense account → the expense account mapped to a category per location: one ShopView Accounts row per category in QuickBooks (S5-R1), one Account Mappings row per category in AccountingHub (S6-R1). Replaces the two fixed rows Internal Work Orders Expense and Customer No-Charge Expense of v0.17.”
  • Feature Overview: “Accounting is one expense account per category. In QuickBooks the accountant maps each category once per location, on the category itself or on the ShopView Accounts page, where the categories show as one row each under Cost of Parts; an empty row posts to ShopView Review as every unmapped row does today, with no fallback to another row. In AccountingHub, Account Mappings holds one row per category, automatically mapped for the starting categories (General Internal to 6500 Vehicle Expenses; Warranty and Goodwill to the existing 6430 Warranty & Goodwill Expense; Comeback to 6440 Comeback Expense). The rollout migration and new-customer setup reuse suitable accounts, create missing required accounts, preserve valid existing mappings and resolve number conflicts with an available number, so all starting mappings are ready before the first job posts (S6-R2); a category the shop adds gets an empty row that holds the event until it is mapped; an archived category keeps its row. The shop supplies credit is unchanged (Story 10). At Close of a whole internal or no-charge work order the parts cost debits the category's account and the credit stays on today's inventory account by part category and stock location. On a billable work order with a no-charge line, that line's parts cost posts to the category's account when the invoice is created; the rest of the work order posts as today.”
  • Key Decisions: “One expense account per category, mapped per location in QuickBooks (as every ShopView Accounts row is) and per organization in AccountingHub (as every Account Mappings row is), with the starting categories mapped automatically in the hub (S6-R2).”

The existing 6400 Shop Equipment Maintenance account remains available for accountants to select where appropriate; it is not an additional starting category. The mapping key should allow a kind (parts, labor) later, so V2 adds rows instead of changing the contract.”
  • Feature Overview: “Accounting is one expense account per category. In QuickBooks the accountant maps each category once per location, on the category itself or on the ShopView Accounts page, where the categories show as one row each under Cost of Parts; an empty row posts to ShopView Review as every unmapped row does today, with no fallback to another row. In AccountingHub, Account Mappings holds one row per category, automatically mapped for the starting categories (General Internal to 6500 Vehicle Expenses; Warranty and Goodwill to the existing 6430 Warranty & Goodwill Expense; Comeback to 6440 Comeback Expense). The rollout migration and new-customer setup reuse suitable accounts, create missing required accounts, preserve valid existing mappings and resolve number conflicts with an available number, so all starting mappings are ready before the first job posts (S6-R2); a category the shop adds gets an empty row that holds the event until it is mapped; an archived category keeps its row. The shop supplies credit is unchanged (Story 10). At Close of a whole internal or no-charge work order the parts cost debits the category's account and the credit stays on today's inventory account by part category and stock location. On a billable work order with a no-charge line, that line's parts cost posts to the category's account when the invoice is created; the rest of the work order posts as today.”

fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The work order shows the status Closed.

Step 3:

  • Two inventory journal entries are found, one per stock part, numbered as invoicing numbers them today.
  • Part A's entry debits account X $80.00 (2 × $40.00) and credits the inventory account the invoice would credit for that part's category and stock location.
  • Part B's entry debits account X $25.00 and credits its inventory account.
  • Nothing is debited to Cost of Parts.
  • Together they post $105.00, the Stock parts figure of the confirmation, with no invoice: no month-end reclass is needed.

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11762 (Story 5, QuickBooks Online account mapping), story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync)

  • S7-R2: “At Close, ShopView sends the inventory journal entries it sends at invoice today (one per picked stock part, same numbering, dated the posting date), with the debit on the expense account of the work order's category instead of the part category's cost of goods sold account or Cost of Parts, and the credit on the same inventory account the invoice would credit today (by part category and stock location). Each entry's memo carries the work order number, the classification and the category. Today these entries are sent only after the QuickBooks invoice synced; Close sends them on its own, with no invoice. The QuickBooks Class of the entry comes from the location of the work order (the mapping the location already uses for its other entries), not from a labor line's labor-rate mapping, which an internal work order does not have; without a Class on the location the entry is sent without one, as today for a part without a labor rate.”
  • Key Decisions: “Part cost goes straight to the expense account, not to cost of goods sold first, one entry per part as invoicing posts today.”
  • Goals: “For a shop on QuickBooks Online or AccountingHub, the month-end reclass journal entry for internal and no-charge jobs is no longer needed.”
  • Terminology: “Category expense account → the expense account mapped to a category per location: one ShopView Accounts row per category in QuickBooks (S5-R1), one Account Mappings row per category in AccountingHub (S6-R1). Replaces the two fixed rows Internal Work Orders Expense and Customer No-Charge Expense of v0.17.”

  • S7-R4: “When a vendor bill was posted to Cost of Parts (or a category account) and the work order later becomes internal or no charge, Close adds a reclass journal entry: debit the mapped expense account, credit the account the bill line was posted to, for that bill's lines. An entry Marked as Exported by hand counts as posted (S7-E2).”
  • S8-E2: “If a work order is reopened while its Close event is Held, the Held event is withdrawn and no reversal is posted (Story 4, S4-E1).”
  • S4-R3: “Confirming reverses exactly the entries that were posted at Close (Stories 7 and 8), returns the parts to inventory as Reverse does today, removes the internal invoice, and sets the work order to Complete with its classification unchanged, the shop supplies amount kept, and the Convert and Change category actions offered again (S2-R9 applies only while closed or invoiced); the green message "Work order [number] reopened" confirms it, as the app confirms other finished actions. The reversal is dated the reopen date, so it is held only if that date's period is closed or missing (S4-E2 is corrected accordingly). Events for one work order are processed in order, one at a time: a Reopen arriving while the Close is Held turns the Close Dismissed; a Dismissed event is never retried and cannot be replayed by hand; a new Close waits while an earlier reversal for the same work order is Held, shown as Held with the reason "Waiting for an earlier held entry of work order [n]", so two Close entries are never posted without the reversal between them.   • S4-R3: “Confirming reverses exactly the entries that were posted at Close (Stories 7 and 8), returns the parts to inventory as Reverse does today, removes the internal invoice, and sets the work order to Complete with its classification unchanged, the shop supplies amount kept, and the Convert and Change category actions offered again (S2-R9 applies only while closed or invoiced); the green message "Work order [number] reopened" confirms it, as the app confirms other finished actions. The reversal is dated the reopen date, so it is held only if that date's period is closed or missing (S4-E2 is corrected accordingly). Events for one work order are processed in order, one at a time: a Reopen arriving while the Close is Held turns the Close Dismissed; a Dismissed event is never retried and cannot be replayed by hand; a new Close waits while an earlier reversal for the same work order is Held, shown as Held with the reason "Waiting for an earlier held entry of work order [n]", so two Close entries are never posted without the reversal between them. Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11766 (Story 9, Reports, dashboard and exports)

  • S9-R1: “Sales, Sales By Customer, Sales By Representative and Advisor Analysis leave whole internal and no-charge work orders out of every number, with no filter and no option to include them. On a billable work order they leave every no-charge line out of labor revenue, parts revenue, labor cost, parts cost, invoiced hours and worked hours, the way a declined line is left out today: the invoice financial snapshot captures the no-charge lines as excluded, and the per-statement queries carry the same condition. The work order itself stays in with its billable amounts. Every dashboard card and ranking (Sales, Sales by Customer, Top Customers with its invoice count, At-Risk Customers, Billing, and the Invoices card, "Total invoices in range") does the same. The dashboard Tech Efficiency card follows the Technician Efficiency report's default (Show all, S9-R3), so the card and the report give the same hours for a technician.”
  • Key Decisions: “One report for free work; the money reports leave internal and no-charge work orders out with no filter.”
  • Goals: “Sales and margin reports exclude internal and no-charge work orders; one report of their own shows them with cost, hours and category.”
  • Feature Overview: “Reports: dollars out, hours in, per work order and per line. Whole internal and no-charge work orders stay out of the money reports as before. A no-charge line on a billable work order is left out the same way by every number that sums revenue, cost, margin, invoiced hours or units per line (Story 9 names each report); its clocked hours stay in the time reports; the work order itself stays in with its billable amounts. The Internal Work Orders report lists whole work orders and single lines with classification, category, original work order and line, original technician, parts cost and hours, with a per-category summary strip and a By technician tab (completed lines, comeback lines, warranty lines, comeback rate, redo hours, redo parts cost).”

  • S10-R1: “An internal or no-charge work order carries one field "Shop supplies" (a dollar amount) in the block where a billable work order shows its totals. It is set when the work order becomes internal or no charge: the customer's Min shop supplies charge from the customer profile, or $0.00 when none is set. The percentage rule and the location percentage do not apply. On a flagged customer, Edit Customer accepts the Min without a shop supplies percentage (today Min is disabled until a percentage is entered); a percentage, if set, never applies to internal or no-charge work orders.”
  • Feature Overview: “Shop supplies are a flat amount. An internal or no-charge work order carries one Shop supplies amount, defaulted from the customer's Min shop supplies charge and editable on the work order until Close. At Close it posts as one entry: debit the work order's expense account, credit the income account of the existing "Shop supplies" item (Products And Services) in QuickBooks, or the existing Shop supplies expense row in AccountingHub. No new mapping row for it. No percentage in this version.”
  • Key Decisions: “Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders are a flat amount, defaulted from the customer's Min shop supplies charge, posted at Close as a debit to the work order's expense account and a credit to the account the shop already maps for shop supplies: in QuickBooks the income account of the existing "Shop supplies" item (Products And Services), in AccountingHub the existing Shop supplies expense row.”

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.4 (13 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 14 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-12226 (Story 12, A no-charge line on a billable work order)

  • S12-R3: “A no-charge line shows the chip "No Charge" next to its title on the lines table, in Tech View and on mobile, with the tooltip "Category: [category]" on hover, as the work order badge has (S2-R16); the category itself is not printed in the chip; Rate, Total and every part on it show $0.00; Margin shows nothing. Hours, technician, status, approval, parts ordering, picking, receiving, clock-ins, notes, inspections and the story work as on any line. The original work order and line are not shown on the line; they are in the notes, the Audit Log, the report and the hub record.”
  • S12-R4: “The work order carries no badge and no header style and its classification stays billable; Financial Info (the cost view) does not change. Totals, tax, work order fees and discounts, deposits, the estimate, the portal approval and the Customer PO are computed on the billable lines; the no-charge line shows at $0.00 on the estimate and in the portal with its category under the title. A line discount on the line is removed when it is marked and not restored by Mark as Billable. A deposit on the work order does not block the mark; when, after the mark, the deposit exceeds the billable total, the dialog says "Deposit $[amount] exceeds the new total $[total]. The difference stays on the customer's account as a deposit when the invoice is created." and the existing rule applies at invoicing. An estimate already on the portal shows the live work order when the customer opens it (same link, no new email; the advisor re-sends when a fresh document is wanted), with the line at $0.00 and its category under the title and the notice "This estimate changed after it was sent. The lines above are current."; a pending IBS request is not withdrawn (ShopView has no withdrawal); as after any price change today, the advisor requests approval again with the new amount when needed. ShopView renders the estimate and invoice documents and the portal shows them; the portal renders its own approval line cards, price summary and emails, where the $0.00 line shows with its category: that portal side is its own story, SV-12296, linked to SV-12226.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “No-charge line | "No Charge" (tooltip "Category: [category]") | Chip next to the line title; Rate, Total and parts at $0.00; Margin empty (S12-R3)”
  • Terminology: “No Charge line → a line of a billable work order marked No Charge with a category. It shows $0.00 on the work order, the estimate, the portal and the invoice; its hours, parts and story stay; its parts cost posts to the category's account when the invoice is created. The work order carries no badge.”
  • Key Decisions: “A no-charge line stays on its billable work order and shows $0.00 on one invoice, instead of moving to a separate work order. One work order, one classification, one document still holds for whole internal and no-charge work orders; the line case is the exception and is handled line by line in the invoice, the posting and every report.”
  • S2-R3: “The work order header shows one badge next to the status: "Internal" for an internal work order, "No Charge" for a no-charge work order (a different style from Internal), in the desktop and the mobile header. It is the only mark on the work order: the customer card on the detail page shows no badge and no category. On the detail page the header card of an internal or no-charge work order has an orange outline and a light orange background (a new style for the header card, on desktop and on the mobile header; the design authority names the token), so the work order is recognised at a glance; there is no hint sentence under the header. The category of a no-charge work order is not shown on the work order; it is in the Change category dialog, on the NO CHARGE document and in the report (S2-R16). A billable work order that carries no-charge lines carries no badge and no header style; the line carries the mark (Story 12).”
